  1. AI is killing All About Berlin

    • AI
    • Economics
    • Search Engines

    806 points · 710 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 06:47 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — The author wrote that AI-driven answer products and search changes were reducing traffic to All About Berlin, threatening the economics of a locally focused information site. The essay described the concern as both a business and web-ecosystem problem.

    Discussion — Commenters debated uncompensated training and answer extraction, creator displacement, concentration of power, and the long-run supply of useful web content. Suggested responses included revenue sharing, regulation, subscriptions, local or open models, and business-model changes.

  2. Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%

    • AI
    • Economics
    • Search Engines

    709 points · 563 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 00:17 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — RevScope argues that Google AI Overviews reduce outbound clicks, citing a randomized desktop-Chrome experiment in which visible Overviews averaged fewer external clicks and estimating an overall organic-click loss. The article combines that working paper with observational Pew and DataForSEO material, states limitations in the modeling and sampling, and finds little demonstrated value in GEO tactics beyond conventional SEO and reputable third-party presence.

    Discussion — The thread debated whether AI answers undermine publishers, hobby communities, and other sources that fund public information, or mainly displace low-value SEO and ad-heavy content. Commenters also discussed copyright, citations, paywalls, revenue sharing, Google’s earlier incentives, and whether search should prioritize direct primary sources; the author acknowledged possible commercial-query bias in one dataset.

  3. What's Next for Nvidia?

    • AI
    • Economics
    • Hardware

    485 points · 588 comments · 15 Nov 2026, 23:55 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Steve Blank argues that Jensen Huang’s reported departure leaves Nvidia exposed to a founder-to-executor transition. He credits Huang with CUDA, the deep-learning pivot, and integrated AI datacenter systems, and says the board needs a successor able to operate today’s business while repeatedly remaking it as hyperscalers develop their own chips.

    Discussion — Discussion both extended and challenged the founder-versus-executor framing. Commenters debated whether Nvidia should cannibalize its GPU business before rivals do, how custom chips and weaker CUDA lock-in could affect margins, and whether Apple and Microsoft are fair post-founder cautionary examples; unverified speculation about the departure was explicitly contested.

  4. Nvidia allegedly engineered scarcity by funding AI startups to buy its GPUs

    • AI
    • Economics
    • Hardware

    1114 points · 651 comments · 14 Nov 2026, 02:52 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — TechPowerUp reported allegations that Nvidia reinforced GPU scarcity by funding AI startups that then bought Nvidia GPUs. The article framed the account as an allegation about incentives and market structure, not an established finding.

    Discussion — Commenters debated the credibility and implications of the allegation, Nvidia’s supply constraints, and whether startup financing can meaningfully distort demand. The thread also discussed competitive dynamics and the economics of AI infrastructure.

    • Economics

    Story — The HN text post reported that U.S. October producer prices rose 6.5% year over year, the highest since November 2022, while the monthly increase was 0.3%; it also cited a revised September annual reading.
